Hold-to-delete ember burn card

I wanted to rebuild Keshav Bagaade's Hold to Delete with HTML-in-canvas, so that the burning page is live DOM rather than a baked bitmap. Edit the key title or notes, then press and hold Hold to delete: an FBM ember front spreads from the button's exact CSS bounding box, cools back intact if you let go early, or burns through to a live Undo delete card at 100%.

Show the code two drawable cards, button-rect SDF, FBM burn shader, quench state and hit-box sync
  1. Two live drawable cards in one canvas. #burn-card holds editable controls and #btn-delete; #deleted-card sits behind it as inert HTML until charge hits 100%.
  2. Measure #btn-delete inside #burn-card. Walks offsetLeft and offsetTop up to #burn-card so uOriginRect matches the rendered button border box and corner distance.
  3. FBM and cellular ember burn shader. Computes rounded-box distance from uOriginRect, warps with 4-octave FBM and thermal updraft, chars ahead of the flame rim and raises sparks over the transparent void.
  4. Hold, quench and reduced-motion state machine. Charges over 1.4 s on pointer or keyboard hold, cools back to zero on early release, and switches to a calm radial wipe without turbulence under reduced motion.
  5. Hit-box sync with geometryUnit(). Flips inert, moves the inactive card offstage with updateElementGeometry() and toggles dataset.hitTick so #btn-undo takes clicks at 100%.
  6. Five-argument 2D and plain-HTML fallbacks. Clips an expanding radial burn ring over #burn-card with five-argument drawElementImage(), or moves both cards into plain HTML if the context is lost.

How it works

This builds on Hold to Delete by Keshav Bagaade. Instead of painting a static snapshot, both the editable card and the recovery card stay live DOM inside one <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree> rendered through ElementGL.

  • Origin from the button box: measureButtonRect() walks offsetLeft and offsetTop from #btn-delete up to #burn-card and computes the farthest corner SDF distance (uMaxDist). In BURN_FRAG, the rounded-box SDF boxSd starts at zero right along the button's CSS border, so even at 4% charge a scorching corona hugs the button before eating outward.
  • Live DOM stays editable mid-burn: typing in the key title or notes, toggling scope pills or pressing Archive triggers a paint event for #burn-card. The listener uploads only the changed element with gl.texElementSubImage2D(), so new letters appear inside the unburnt paper and char as you scrub past them.
  • Quench vs commit: releasing pointer or Space/Enter before 1.4 s keeps deleted = false and cools charge back to zero at 1.65 units per second, leaving everything you typed intact. Completing 100% marks #burn-card inert and offstage, calls updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit(), toggles dataset.hitTick and hands pointer and keyboard focus to Undo delete.
  • Touch scroll and reduced motion: only #btn-delete uses touch-action: none (with context menu suppressed on long press) so normal scrolling over the rest of the card still works on a phone. When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set, the shader skips FBM turbulence, heat shimmer and sparks and steps the circular progress ring cleanly.
  • Fallbacks: without WebGL 2 texElementSubImage2D(), the canvas falls back to a 2D context clipping a radial burn hole over five-argument drawElementImage(). On webglcontextlost or unsupported browsers, both cards move into plain HTML until restored.

Findings

Not verified yet in headless Chromium 157 or Chrome 159 on Android. Tap "Run these 5 checks" above to measure this browser.

  • Not verified yet: live texElementSubImage2D() ember shader rendering, ray-sampled char and flame front values at charge = 0.55, updateElementGeometry() hit-testing on #btn-undo, touch long-press stability at 412 px and webglcontextlost recovery in Chromium 157 or Chrome 159 on Android.
  • Button-box coordinates vs intermediate flex rows: putting position: relative only on #burn-card (and keeping flex rows position: static) lets offsetLeft and offsetTop map straight to texture pixels without waiting on getBoundingClientRect() during layout changes.
  • Premultiplied transparency behind the flame front: fading rising spark particles inside burnGap > -0.20 keeps the burned void deep behind the front at strict alpha = 0 so the recovery card underneath shows cleanly and shader tests can verify transparency inside the button rectangle.
  • In-card DOM updates throttled to 5% steps: updating the card's internal percentage badge and progress bar every 5% instead of every 16 ms avoids repainting the DOM on every animation frame while keeping the WebGL flame running at display refresh rate.
